what: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico runs 12 airports in western Mexico, including Guadalajara, Tijuana and the resort airports at Puerto Vallarta and Los Cabos, plus two in Jamaica.
customers: Airlines paying per passenger, and passengers spending in the terminals.
moat: A fifty-year concession to run each airport, with tariffs set in five-year reviews. Nobody builds a competing airport next door.
risks: Mexican regulators reset the tariff formula every five years and the last review was unfavourable
Passenger numbers depend on American tourism to Mexico, which follows the United States economy
Required capital spending is set by the concession, not by the company
opportunities: A 23.1% net margin and revenue up from $931M to $2.2B in four years
Traffic through Guadalajara and Tijuana grows with Mexican manufacturing, not just tourism
Commercial revenue per passenger has room to rise toward international levels
watch: Passenger traffic growth and the outcome of tariff reviews.
